articles.headline: Rueben Chinyelu comes up big and No. 3 Florida escapes with a 76-67 win against Milwaukee
articles.description: — Rueben Chinyelu posted his first double-double of the season and made the first 3-pointer of his college career as No. 3 Florida escaped with a 76-67 victory against Milwaukee on Tuesday night.

articles.headline: Colorado rallies from 20-point deficit, beats Stanford 70-65 at Acrisure Series
articles.description: — Barrington Hargress had 19 points on 7-of-8 shooting, Justin Neely scored 16 and Colorado overcame a 20-point deficit and beat Stanford 70-65 on Tuesday night at the Acrisure Series.

articles.headline: No. 22 Gonzaga routs Kansas State 101-61 in Players Era 16 first round
articles.description: — Massamba Diop scored 18 points and grabbed seven rebounds as No. 22 Gonzaga routed Kansas State 101-61 on Tuesday night in the opening round of the Players Era 16 tournament.

articles.headline: Louisville's Kelsey tells 5th-year critics 'bring it' as Trimble shines in upset
articles.description: After Seth Trimble led Louisville to a 72-64 win over No. 5 Texas Tech, Cardinals coach Pat Kelsey told critics of teams using fifth-year players, "Everybody can have their opinion. Bring it."

images.name: Seth Trimble [600x400]
images.caption: Seth Trimble scored 24 points in Tuesday's win over No. 5 Texas Tech that gave Louisville its first victory over an AP top-five opponent under coach Pat Kelsey.

articles.headline: No. 13 St. John's beats Oregon 90-79 in opening round of Players Era 16 tournament
articles.description: — Ian Jackson scored 21 points as part of a balanced effort by No. 13 St. John's, which beat Oregon 90-79 on Tuesday night in the opening round of the Players Era 16 tournament.

article.story: LOUISVILLE, Ky. -- — Flory Bidunga scored 17 of his career high-tying 25 points in the first half and No. 23 Louisville shut down Stetson after halftime for an 83-69 win on Thursday night. Adrian Wooley pitched in 14 of his 19 points before halftime as the Cardinals (3-1) overcame an early eight-point deficit. Stetson (1-5), a team coming off back-to-back 20-loss seasons and predicted to finish sixth in the Atlantic Sun Conference this season, made nine of its first 12 shots. A jumper by Thiago Sucatzky capped a 15-2 run and gave the Hatters a 22-14 lead with 11:27 left in the half. The Cardinals recovered behind the work of Wooley and Bidunga, who stepped up after leading scorer Seth Trimble was a late scratch due to a minor injury. Bidunga scored the next seven points to trim the deficit to one, and after the Hatters responded, Wooley scored five in a six-point surge for Louisville. His layup tied the game at 27 with 6:55 left. Louisville led 42-34 in the final minute of the half before Mangus Entenmann's 3-pointer cut the Cardinals' halftime advantage to five. The Cardinals made 15 of 30 shots in the first half, with Bidunga going 6 for 8 and Wooley going 6 for 10. The Hatters missed 18 of 20 shots over a nine-minute stretch of the second half. That allowed the Cardinals to expand a six-point lead to 70-45 after Bidunga's dunk with 10:13 remaining. Karter Knox, who started for Trimble, scored all of his 14 points in the second half for Louisville and grabbed 10 rebounds. Collin Kuhl, the preseason ASUN player of the year, led the Hatters with 24. Entenmann finished with 15 and Sucatzky contributed 10. Up next Stetson plays at South Florida next Tuesday. Louisville travels to Las Vegas for the Players Era Tournament, with its first matchup against ninth-ranked Texas Tech. ------ Sign up for Top 25 poll alerts here, visit the Top 25 here and see AP’s full men’s basketball coverage here
